purpose: Check whether distances between encoded real future trajectories preserve ordering of errors in selected task geometry.
reference: Each real condition-candidate future trajectory in turn.
alternatives: All other real condition-candidate trajectories from the same source scene; exclude identity.
supplementary_alternatives: Other actions under the same hidden condition.
distance: Mean over five times of squared Euclidean error; selected physical coordinates or full native target latent. No goal costs.
ordering_tolerance: 1e-8 + 1e-7 * max(abs(distance_a), abs(distance_b)), separately in each distance space; numerical tolerance only.
primary_reversal_rate: reversed comparisons / comparisons with neither physical nor latent numerical ties; aggregate within scene, then average scenes.
tie_reporting: Report physical tie counts and latent tie fraction among physical-strict comparisons; do not interpret all-tie as perfect ordering.
large_error_contrast: Physical RMS errors differ by at least factor two and larger RMS is >=1 task unit (px-equivalent or mm); diagnostic effect-size subset, not accuracy acceptance.
uncertainty: 4000 source-cluster bootstrap samples, seed 20261008; mirrored Damping scenes together.

physical_scope.pusht: Agent xy, block xy, 40*sin(theta), 40*cos(theta), pixels-equivalent. Selected pose geometry, not full state.
physical_scope.mass: Fingertip xy in millimetres, not all joint states.

dino_excluded: Cached 4x4 pooled patch features are not the native 16x16 patch space used by the benchmark score.
limits: This does not use model predictions or test history utilization.
True-target ordering consistency is not sufficient to validate off-manifold predicted latent physical error.
Rendering/visibility and selected physical coordinates can cause discrepancies; do not attribute all reversals to the encoder.
No fixed acceptance threshold or new benchmark score is introduced.
